summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported from Cincinnati that arrangements for the Allen-Goss fight were complete and Allen had left for the battle ground, while Joe Coburn said the fight was fixed for Goss to get the money.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Dispatch, Wednesday Evening, September 6, 1876 (Last Edition, 5 P.M.). Predates the 1878 Post-Dispatch merger.

facts.fact: Arrangements for the Allen-Goss fight were completed at Cincinnati and Allen left for the fighting ground ahead of Goss
Allen was to fight Joe Goss at about 178 pounds to Goss's 164, seconded by Tom Kelly of St. Louis and Arthur Chambers of Philadelphia; Goss by Jem Mace and Joe Coburn
Joe Coburn said that although Allen was the better man, the fight would be fixed for Goss to get the money; Tom Kelly wired St. Louis that Allen would not get fair play

notes: Jack Looney of St. Louis arrived with a party of 25 men saying Allen must be whipped.
